newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa arrests Briton accused of fake bomb claim.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa arrests Briton accused of fake bomb claim.

text.p: A British man has been arrested on a charge of falsely telling Johannesburg International Airport staff that he had a bomb in his luggage, South African police said on Tuesday.
The fake claim led to a four-hour delay of the Johannesburg to London flight late on Saturday night while police searched all the passengers' luggage, Captain Kamal Shivanand said in a statement.
Michael Kaye, of Dewsbury in West Yorkshire, was travelling with a woman friend. The pair was prevented from boarding the flight when problems were identified with one of their visas.

"It is alleged that Mr Kaye proceeded to client services where he reported that there was a bomb in his suitcase, which was already on the plane. The suspect was warned that this was an offence but he insisted that there was a bomb on the plane," Shivanand said.

The flight was stopped on the runway and all the baggage checked. Police said one suitcase was initially unaccounted for, and was later found to belong to Kaye's travelling companion. However, no bomb was found in any of the bags on the plane.
Kaye was arrested under civil aviation regulations and released on bail of 3,000 rand ($537) after a brief hearing in the Kempton Park Magistrate's Court, pending a trial date.
